title: jnana: the Brahma Sutras 1.1–1.4 with Shankara

segments.voice: Yesterday, jnana reached the fourth sutra: the Upanishads point together at Brahman, and knowing it is a seeing, not a task. Today the sutras test that on one odd line.

A hand laid flat on the chest finds it right away: a steady knock, keeping time. Deep in the Katha Upanishad there's a stranger measurement for that spot. A person the size of a thumb, the text says, stands in the middle of the body. Lord of what was and what will be. Like a flame without smoke. Read quickly, it sounds like a tiny being living behind the ribs. The Brahma Sutras stop at this line and ask something plain. Who is this, exactly? A small soul, or Brahman itself?
screen: `A STEADY KNOCK BEHIND THE RIBS.` → `A PERSON THE SIZE OF A THUMB.` → `A SMALL SOUL, OR BRAHMAN?`

segments.voice: The sutra answers from the words themselves. Look at the title the Upanishad gives: lord of past and future. A soul caught in one life doesn't rule what was and what will be. That title belongs to Brahman. So, the sutra says, the thumb-sized one is Brahman. Then why so small? The next sutra gives the reason, and Shankara opens it up: the measure belongs to the heart. Brahman is spoken of as thumb-sized because that's where the text points the seeker to find it, in the space of the heart. Shankara reaches for an everyday picture. The space inside a hollow reed takes the reed's measure. It's still just space, as wide as all the rest. That's how jnana reads here. It doesn't add a tiny creature to the chest. It recognizes the boundless where it's met. And the Upanishad says one more thing about that person: it's the same today and tomorrow. The flame doesn't flicker with the days. Other Vedanta teachers read these sutras in their own way; here we're following Shankara.
screen: `LORD OF PAST AND FUTURE.` · `THE MEASURE BELONGS TO THE HEART.` · `SPACE IN A REED IS STILL SPACE.` · then, large: `THE BOUNDLESS, MET IN THE HEART.`

segments.voice: Lay one hand flat on the middle of your chest and feel it rise and fall. Notice the heartbeat under your palm, if you can find it, and the warmth where hand meets shirt. Then widen your attention to the space of the whole room, and notice that the space inside the chest and the space outside aren't two different kinds. If you pray, you can rest there with the one the text calls lord of past and future; if not, just rest in the width.
Jnana: knowledge that frees. Here, it reads a thumb-sized person in the heart as Brahman, met where the seeker looks.
Your line: jnana: the Brahma Sutras 1.1–1.4 with Shankara, where space in a reed is still space. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: In Advaita Vedanta, the thumb-sized person of the Katha Upanishad is read as Brahman pointed out in the heart, and some teachers use the space of the heart as a place to turn attention during meditation.
